The *Paccuppannavāra* ("Section on the Present") is a canonical Abhidhamma text situated within the *Yamaka* ("The Book of Pairs"), where it forms sub-section Ya 5.3.1 of the *Saccayamaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text applies the distinctive paired question-and-answer format of the *Yamaka* to investigate the noble truths (*sacca*) specifically in relation to the present period of time (*paccuppanna*) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one translation in one language for this section [SuttaCentral].

Its largest reuse partners belong to the *Anusayayamaka*, specifically the *Pajahanavāra* (Ya 7.2.3; 41 matches, 2,305 characters) and the *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4; 28 matches, 2,647 characters) [DharmaNexus]. Strong internal parallels also appear across related sections within the *Saccayamaka*, including the *Nirodhavāra* (Ya 5.2.2; 9 matches, 1,138 characters), the *Atītānāgatavāra* (Ya 5.3.6), the *Atītavāra* (Ya 5.3.2), the *Paccuppannānāgatavāra* (Ya 5.3.5), and the *Paccuppannātītavāra* (Ya 5.3.4), as well as corresponding temporal sections in other Yamaka chapters such as the *Paccuppannavāra* of the *Āyatanayamaka* (Ya 3.3.1) and the *Khandhayamaka* (Ya 2.3.1) [DharmaNexus].
